text_blocks.snippet: For microsatellite stable (MSS) colon cancer, the primary treatment approach is typically chemotherapy and surgery, with immunotherapy showing limited success on its own. Recent advancements, however, are exploring combination therapies that include immunotherapy for MSS colon cancer, particularly in cases resistant to chemotherapy.

list.title: Surgery:
list.snippet: For early-stage MSS colon cancer (Stages I-II), surgical resection is often curative, with high 5-year survival rates.

list.title: Chemotherapy:
list.snippet: For Stage III and IV, adjuvant chemotherapy (following surgery) and chemotherapy in the metastatic setting are standard, often using regimens like FOLFOX (5-FU, leucovorin, and oxaliplatin). Targeted therapies like bevacizumab and cetuximab may also be used in advanced cases.

list.title: Chemotherapy and Immunotherapy Combinations:
list.snippet: Research is investigating the potential of combining chemotherapy with immunotherapy, such as using chemotherapy to potentially improve the tumor microenvironment and make it more susceptible to immunotherapy.

list.title: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors:
list.snippet: While traditionally ineffective in MSS colon cancer due to the tumors being "immune cold", combinations of checkpoint inhibitors (like botensilimab and balstilimab) are showing promise in some patients resistant to chemotherapy.

list.title: Targeted Therapies with Immunotherapy:
list.snippet: Combining immunotherapy with targeted therapies like anti-angiogenic agents (e.g., bevacizumab) and BRAF inhibitors (in BRAF-mutated tumors) is also being explored.

list.title: Dual Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors:
list.snippet: Combinations of different checkpoint inhibitors (e.g., CTLA-4 and PD-1 inhibitors) are being investigated to overcome the limitations of single-agent immunotherapy.

list.title: Other Immunotherapy Combinations:
list.snippet: Research is also exploring the use of immunotherapy in combination with radiotherapy and other approaches aimed at converting "cold" tumors into "hot" tumors (more susceptible to immunotherapy).

list.title: Liver Metastases:
list.snippet: The presence of active liver metastases can impact the effectiveness of immunotherapy in MSS colon cancer.

list.title: Biomarkers:
list.snippet: Research is ongoing to identify biomarkers that can predict which patients will respond best to immunotherapy in MSS colon cancer.

list.title: Clinical Trials:
list.snippet: Many of the immunotherapy approaches mentioned are still being evaluated in clinical trials, and patients may need to consider participating in trials to access these treatments.
